_: The fifteen V90Phase4Modulator state-machine edges, against t_v90p4mgen.
The claims worth attacking are WHICH state each member guards on, WHICH
divisor the boundary test uses, WHICH state it hands on to on and off a
boundary, the sense of each latch, and the five copies of the Ed block
and three of the CPd block being separate copies rather than one.
Several bodies are textually identical between members, so every anchor
below carries enough surrounding lines to name its own function.  That
is rule 1 of tools/anchorcheck.py and it is why the labels can be trusted

recivedPartTwoSilenceRrnSUV: the first range guard is dropped
why: DEAD BY CONSTRUCTION, and its survival is the measurement of that rather than a gap.  The body is guarded by `state == P4M_STATE_SUVD` (5), so the two range guards -- 0x17..0x18 and 0x19..0x1b -- can never be the difference between running it and not: no state satisfies both.  The object HAS them, in that order, and dropping either changes the instruction sequence and nothing else, which is why they are written out and why no differential trial can adjudicate them.  The codegen tier is what holds them: with the guard gone the function is no longer identical to .text+0x2ca50.  The SECOND guard is not equivalent and is caught, because the mutation there widens it to swallow SUVd itself.
